title: What the far-pair sign decides, and where it stops
claim: For a fill with a middle knot B(p,r,q), a near end knot B(a,p,r) and a far end knot B(c,d,r): L1 the moved splits are those with a, not q, not d on p's side; L2 two old splits come to cross iff one is moved, the other not, and the unmoved one's p-side lies inside the moved one's; L3-L4 under the far-pair sign (every crossed split separates c from d) clause (a) holds, the new crossings are G x M and r sides with d on every crossed split; L5 under the sign a crossing-making fill is a copy step iff no uncrossed split is moved and the moved splits are the crossers of one unmoved crossed split, on a base of two orders iff they are one whole order; L6 a pair pattern (crossed splits all separate p from q, none separates a from p, some but not all separate p from d) gives the copy step; Proposition 7: on a seven-distinction base of two orders, the sign without the copy step and the copy step without the sign. The equivalence on SEEDK's knot-local fills (F1, T1, T2) is not proved.
standard_statement: Split systems, compatibility and crossing; half-spaces of median graphs.
prior_work: COPY-CLASS-20261118-001 (referee R1's sign and its half 'sign implies (a)'); MID-RULE-20261118-001 (E1); COPY-READ-20261118-001 (copy class); Bandelt and Dress (1992); Eppstein (2005).
completion_gate: Ticket B scores F1, T1, T2 and the sign against SEED on fresh runs and reproduces Proposition 7; the referee reviews.
